newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Germany wants strict version of Maastricht - Stark.
newsitem.headline: Germany wants strict version of Maastricht - Stark.

text.p: Germany wants a "clear, hard, strict and narrow" interpretation of the Maastricht treaty when deciding which countries can join European monetary union in 1999, finance ministry number two Juergen Stark said on Monday.

Stark, at a meeting of European Union finance ministers in Luxembourg, also said that one-off fiscal consolidation in 1997 to comply with Maastricht would not be enough "in a historical project of these dimensions."

"We want a clear, hard, strict and narrow interpretation of the criteria," Stark said in remarks apparently directed at southern European countries which have mounted belated efforts to consolidated their 1997 budgets.

Judgement falls next year on EU states wanting to join the planned launch of the single currency in 1999. Maastricht sets a budget deficit limit of three percent of gross domestic product and a state debt ceiling of 60 percent of GDP, even though the treaty leaves scope for looser interpretation.
Stark said: "We will look at all these elements very carefully -- firstly how far they agree with the treaty and secondly if they mesh with sustainable budget consolidation.
"A decision cannot be reached through a one-off result in the target year which starts a historic project of these dimensions," Stark said, saying that consolidation must continue after 1997.
